describes: US sales tax determination: what is charged, and why.

dataset.name: us-tax-dataset
dataset.why: Eight states — CA, FL, HI, KS, NC, PA, TX, VA — chosen to carry the cases that have actually gone wrong here, not to be representative. Pinned rather than live for the same reason as the EU corpus: a rate that changes in the world must not silently change what a vector asserts.

vectors.pins: A bare state code gives the state's rate and NOTHING BELOW IT, and the engine says so rather than implying precision it does not have: the confidence is derived, not authoritative, and the rate carries NoLocalResolution. This vector was originally written to assert the opposite — that Florida is county-resolved, which it is — and it proved nothing, because a query with no address detail has no county to resolve. Precision comes from what you ASK, not from which state you are in.

A facilitated sale charges nothing because the marketplace already collected. The treatment must say MarketplaceFacilitated — Exempt and NotRegistered are the same zero and mean opposite things on a return, and a facilitated sale is none of the others: the tax WAS due and somebody else owed it.

The marketplace's liability is not derived from the seller's presence. A seller with no registration in the state still owes nothing on a facilitated sale — and the reason must say why, because NotRegistered would say something else entirely about the same zero.

THE OPPOSITE OF THE EU RULE, AND WORTH STATING BESIDE IT. Without nexus a US seller has no authority to collect, so charging would be collecting tax nobody is owed. In the EU the same empty registration list means a distance seller is non-compliant and must still charge. One engine, two regimes, two answers — which is why the corpus carries both.

The breakdown exists to show a stack — state, county, city, transit district — and a state-only answer has no stack to show. Emitting a single-component breakdown would dress an unresolved answer up as a resolved one, which is the same lie the confidence field exists to prevent.

Texas exempts clothing priced 'less than $100', so $99.99 is exempt and exactly $100.00 is taxed. Florida's statute says '$100 or less' and exempts it. The engine defaults caps to EXCLUSIVE because that is the direction that over-collects, and a wrong boundary here is off by the whole line rather than by a rounding unit.

The same shirt a cent cheaper, the same weekend, is exempt — and the treatment says Exempt rather than a zero rate, because the state did not set the rate to nothing, it removed the supply from tax for three days.

Dates are the whole mechanism. The identical shirt on the 1st of August is taxed, because the window had not opened — and a holiday resolved at today's date instead of the supply's would exempt every backdated invoice raised during one.
